local.title: Older Burton hedges need **thinning out.**
local.intro: Most Burton homes were built in the 1950s and 60s, and many of the foundation shrubs around them are nearly as old. Years of shearing only the outside leave a hedge green on the surface and bare inside, and some shrubs now cover the windows.

points.title: Timing by the plant
points.body: MSU Extension says lilac, forsythia, spirea, weigela and viburnum bloom on buds set the summer before, so they get shaped right after they flower. Other shrubs follow a different calendar, and we sort that out on the walkthrough.

points.title: Thinning a crowded hedge
points.body: MSU Extension notes that taking out a few crowded stems each year opens the middle of a shrub to light and air and cuts down on mildew. On an old Burton hedge, a little thinning every year does more good than another hard shear.

points.title: Clear of the walk and the drive
points.body: Shrubs that crowd the sidewalk catch snow and make the city's 24 hour clearing rule harder to keep, and shrubs at the end of the drive block the view of the street. We keep both cut back.

points.title: Removing a shrub past saving
points.body: Some old shrubs are past trimming. We dig those out, roots and all, and the bed can start over with something sized for the spot. See [bush removal](/bush-removal/) for how that goes.

logistics.title: How shrub trimming works in Burton.
body: Rob walks the beds with you, names what is growing there and says when each one should be cut. Some yards need one visit a year and others two, depending on what is planted.

The crew shapes each shrub and hedge to a clean line with hand pruners and trimmers, thins crowded stems where it helps, rakes the clippings out of the beds and hauls them away. Walks and the drive get blown off before we leave.

Clippings leave in our trailer rather than going out for EMTERRA yard waste pickup. Trimming pairs well with a [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-burton-mi/) or a [fall cleanup](/leaf-removal-burton-mi/) visit.

faq.q: Do you trim shrubs and hedges in Burton, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes trims shrubs and hedges in Burton, shaping them back to clean lines at the right time for each plant and hauling the clippings away. Overgrown bushes can be dug out instead. The estimate is free.

faq.q: When should I trim my hedges in Michigan?
faq.a: It depends on the plant. MSU Extension says spring bloomers such as lilac, forsythia, spirea and weigela should be pruned right after they finish flowering, because they set next year's buds the summer before. Dead branches can come out in early spring on almost anything.

faq.q: Can an overgrown shrub be cut back hard?
faq.a: Some can and some cannot, and it depends on the plant. Rob will tell you which kind you have when he sees it. When a shrub is past saving, [bush removal](/bush-removal/) and a fresh planting is often the better call.

faq.q: Do you take away the clippings?
faq.a: Yes. Everything we cut gets raked out of the beds and hauled off in our trailer, so the beds are left clean and you have nothing to bundle for the curb.
